id: title:jose-sequeira:bound writer upsert concurrency and pace flush drains

review.posthog_relevance: Adds a permit semaphore and configuration to bound concurrent chunk execution and saturation tracking, potentially preventing database connection pool exhaustion and improving reliability of person identity ingestion.
review.reason: The chunk includes implementation of a permit semaphore and its use in chunk execution, along with configuration and saturation tracking. This could help prevent database connection pool exhaustion, which could lead to degraded performance or failures in the PostHog system.
review.uncertainty: The chunk does not include the complete implementation of the permit semaphore, the semaphore type, or the full WriterTask implementation. This makes it impossible to assess the complete implementation and its relationship to the permit semaphore and the OffsetCommitter trait implementation.

observations.behavior: Documentation change: flush interval, buffer size, backpressure, and saturation counters documented. No score.
observations.code_quote: Every flush drains at most `FLUSH_BUFFER_SIZE` rows (rounded up to whole partitions), so a backlogged buffer empties as a sequence of bounded batches paced by the writer instead of one giant batch. Whole partitions only: a partition's max offset is safe to commit exactly when every buffered person from it has flushed, so a drained batch's offsets never skip past a person still in the buffer.
observations.posthog_connection: This documents a change to the person identity writer's batching and backpressure behavior. The implementation is not supplied, so no score.

observations.behavior: Documentation change: transient and saturation failure handling documented. No score.
observations.code_quote: - **Saturation** (local pool acquire timeout): the writer's own in-flight statements exceeded pool capacity — self-inflicted, so it retries with the same backoff but never counts toward the consecutive-failure shutdown. Escalating on it would let a slow-PG burst crash-loop the pod, and each restart drops the buffers and redelivers, worsening the load that caused it.
observations.posthog_connection: This documents a change to the person identity writer's transient and saturation failure handling. The implementation is not supplied, so no score.

observations.behavior: Documentation change: backpressure and concurrency limits documented. No score.
observations.code_quote: Total in-flight statement concurrency is capped by a pod-wide permit budget (`UPSERT_CONCURRENCY`) shared across all writer lanes and both the chunk and per-row paths. A burst of chunks queues at the semaphore — a cheap, unbounded wait — instead of oversubscribing the pool and converting its own fan-out into acquire timeouts.
